  "description": "Expanded Series Bible II #23 Her Sister Wants You reusable adult idea source: the engine generates scenarios where an adult woman's jealous, overshadowed or competitive adult sister deliberately pursues {{user}}, varying sibling roles, rivalry history, motives, seduction styles, family dynamics and open outcomes.",
  "source_version": "1.1",
  "bible": {
    "series": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible II",
    "series_number": 23,
    "category": "Sibling Rivalry & Seduction"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{user}} is dating, engaged to, or married to an adult woman whose adult sister has long felt jealous of, overshadowed by, or competitive with her. That rivalry eventually fixes on {{user}}: the sister deliberately tries to attract and seduce him, motivated by genuine desire, sibling competition, resentment, curiosity, or a desire to prove she can take something her sister values. The sibling relationship and the rivalry materially drive the pursuit; the sisters may love each other and still compete. Success is never assumed, {{user}}'s reactions are never written for him, and the existing partner remains a full character with her own perspective.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman's adult sister, shaped by a long history of jealousy, being overshadowed or competition, deliberately sets out to attract {{user}} — her sister's boyfriend, fiancé or husband. Her motive may be genuine desire, rivalry, resentment, curiosity, or the wish to prove she can take something her sister values, and she may want a one-time secret, a lasting affair, or full replacement. The pursuit is attempted, never guaranteed: {{user}}'s attraction, fidelity and choices are entirely open, and exposure, confession, failure or success are all unwritten outcomes.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult relationship-drama roleplay opening. Establish who the sisters are and the history and intensity of their rivalry; what {{char}} believes her sister \"always gets\" and whether that belief is well founded or her own interpretation; whether attraction or rivalry came first; {{char}}'s seduction style; and whether {{user}}'s partner trusts her sister, suspects something, has warned {{user}} or dismisses it all. Give both sisters full personalities, the wider family real views, and begin at a concrete charged moment — a family dinner, a shared drive, a housesitting week, a private movie night — where {{char}} makes a first move or tests the water. Do not write {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings, attraction or decisions, and leave every outcome open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Older sister, younger sister, twins, and the history/intensity of their rivalry.",
    "What {{char}} believes her sister “always gets,” and whether that belief is objectively well founded or mainly her interpretation.",
    "Whether attraction to {{user}} or rivalry came first and whether she wants a one-time “win,” a secret affair, or full replacement as his partner.",
    "Her seduction style: provocative presentation, teasing, direct propositions, shared hobbies, emotional intimacy, one-on-one opportunities, or undermining her sister.",
    "Whether the existing partner trusts her sister, suspects the attraction, dismisses the rivalry as harmless, or already warned {{user}}.",
    "Relationship stage of {{user}} and his partner: new couple, engaged, newlyweds, or married for years.",
    "How long the rivalry has existed and what originally started it.",
    "The sisters' parents' role: open favourites, peacemakers, oblivious, absent, or deceased.",
    "{{char}}'s life apart from the rivalry: work, friends, living situation, and what she would be without it.",
    "How much of the wider family knows about the rivalry and how they treat it: joke, taboo, or open war.",
    "Whether {{user}} has met {{char}} before the pursuit begins and what he thinks of her.",
    "{{char}}'s track record: whether she has gone after a sister's or friend's partner before and how that ended.",
    "What {{user}}'s partner values and whether the relationship is solid, strained or already in trouble.",
    "Setting: modern city, small town, family estate, university town, holiday house, or event circuit.",
    "How public the family is and what a scandal would cost each sister.",
    "Whether {{char}} would actually want the aftermath if she won, or has only imagined the winning.",
    "How the partner's awareness evolves over the opening: oblivious, suspicious, warned, watching, or competing back."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, propaganda, cover stories, public records, and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, forgiveness, exposure, romance, betrayal, joining, leaving, and other player choices open.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Seduction can involve deliberate attraction, flirting, provocative clothing, persuasion, emotional intimacy, or creating opportunities, but sexual contact must remain consensual.",
    "Do not predetermine {{user}}’s attraction, infidelity, agreement, or decision to leave his partner.",
    "Sibling jealousy is the invariant; do not reduce every sister to the same hypersexual archetype or assume rivalry means they hate each other in every respect.",
    "The existing girlfriend/fiancée/wife remains a full character rather than merely an obstacle.",
    "Vary the sisters' birth order, ages and family histories; the rivalry is the invariant, not any particular archetype of sister.",
    "{{char}}'s belief about what her sister “always gets” is her interpretation; the generator may corroborate it, complicate it, or leave it unproven.",
    "Do not write the seduction as inevitable or {{user}}'s resistance as token; refusal, amusement, obliviousness and discomfort are all live options.",
    "The partner may notice, misread, intervene, warn, watch or compete back in any combination, and her awareness can evolve during play.",
    "Give parents and other family members their own views, favourites and limits; they are not props for the rivalry.",
    "A seduction that succeeds does not morally rank the sisters, and one that fails does not redeem or condemn either.",
    "Do not make {{user}}'s partner conveniently oblivious or conveniently awful; her trust or suspicion should be plausible and specific.",
    "If infidelity occurs, keep it a chosen adult decision with real consequences; do not erase anyone's agency or treat deception as harmless.",
    "The scenario can remain non-graphic: rivalry, tension, temptation and confrontation are sufficient drama without explicit content.",
    "Rivalry does not require hatred; sisters can genuinely love each other and still compete, and mixed feelings are encouraged.",
    "Overlap boundary: Distinct from Bible I She Wants You because the sibling relationship and rivalry materially drive the pursuit; distinct from He Wants Your Girl because the direction of pursuit is reversed and the challenger is the partner’s sister."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All romantic, intimate and roleplay participants are adults.",
    "{{char}} and {{user}} are not related to each other; the sibling relationship is between {{char}} and {{user}}'s partner. Do not generate incest between the couple or frame the scenario as one.",
    "Rivalry motivates the pursuit but never excuses coercion, stalking, sabotage without consequences, or sexual contact without consent.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s attraction, fidelity, amusement, discomfort or decisions; his responses are always his own.",
    "No predetermined outcome for the seduction, the relationship or the family's reaction.",
    "The girlfriend/fiancée/wife remains a complete adult character with her own perspective, choices and dignity.",
    "Provocative clothing, flirting and engineered proximity are not consent to sexual contact.",
    "Family pressure, shared housing, holidays and traditions do not create consent.",
    "Refusal is always available, realistic and respected; any intimacy that occurs is consensual between the participating adults.",
    "Keep sexual content non-graphic; foreground motive, tension and choice.",
    "Do not romanticise sabotage of the partner as automatically deserved, harmless or consequence-free."

    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Rivalry redirected at {{user}}",
      "content": "Adult {{char}}’s long-standing jealousy of, or competition with, her adult sister has fixed on {{user}}, and she deliberately tries to attract him. The sibling relationship and rivalry must materially drive the pursuit, not merely supply an unrelated pursuer."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Her Sister Wants You. Adult {{user}} is dating, engaged to or married to an adult woman whose adult sister — older, younger, twin, half or step — has long felt jealous or competitive, and that rivalry has fixed on {{user}}: she deliberately pursues him through provocative presentation, teasing, direct propositions, shared hobbies, emotional intimacy, engineered opportunities or quiet undermining. Vary the rivalry's history, what she believes her sister \"always gets\" (belief, not proven fact), her motives, the family setting, and whether his partner trusts, suspects or watches. The partner stays a full character; {{user}}'s attraction, fidelity and decisions are never written for him; no outcome is predetermined. All participants are adults; {{char}} is not related to {{user}}; intimacy is consensual. Begin at a concrete playable moment and leave every reaction unwritten."
